Tagalog ('Sa kabilugan, nakikita natin ang buong mukha nito na naliliwanagan, kaya mukha itong bilog at maliwanag!') and Cebuano ('Sa takdol, makita nato ang tibuok nawong niini nga nahayagan, mao nga morag lingin ug hayag kini!') are faithful, natural, and grade-appropriate. Verified against EarthSky: during full moon the Moon's entire sunlit near side faces Earth, which is exactly why it looks fully round and bright. Single variant, no textual differences to reconcile. Parent consolidation verification: Seeing the full sunlit face explains the observed full-Moon appearance. Only moon admitted; translations retain the illumination relationship. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20014.review.jsonl

fungi-digest-not-plant-misconception-g6.notes: The card teaches the exact criterion textbooks use to place fungi in their own group apart from plants (no chlorophyll, cannot photosynthesize, must obtain food from other organisms) — this is a genuine classification characteristic for G5-L-4's 'microorganisms including fungi' group, not a bare mention of the word 'fungi'. The only other candidates that superficially match (e.g. G4-L-1 digestive facet via the word 'digest') would only be reached by keyword hijack since the card is about fungal nutrition, not the human digestive system, so they were rejected. Tagalog/Cebuano are faithful, natural, and grade-appropriate. The claim (fungi lack chlorophyll and are heterotrophic) is standard, well-established biology. Parent consolidation verification: Absence of chlorophyll and heterotrophic digestion distinguish fungi from plants, without restricting every fungus to dead matter. Translations preserve classification mechanism. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20014.review.jsonl

fungi-kingdom-classification-g6.notes: This card is a near-ideal fit: it directly teaches that fungi are neither plants nor animals but their own classification group, with a concrete distinguishing characteristic (chitin vs. cellulose cell walls) — exactly the kind of characteristic-based grouping G5-L-4 asks students to build a table around for 'microorganisms including fungi'. Other keyword-matched candidates (G7-L-4 cell-wall facet, G9-M-5 ion formation via 'gain', G10-L-6 biotechnology via 'organism/cell') do not genuinely teach their respective competencies and were rejected as hijacks. Translations are faithful and age-appropriate. The claim (Kingdom Fungi, chitin cell walls vs. plant cellulose) is standard, correct biology. Parent consolidation verification: Separate fungal kingdom and chitin versus plant cellulose give explicit classification characteristics. All languages preserve both distinctions. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20014.review.jsonl

fungi-mycoprotein-quorn-g8.notes: The card gives a concrete, correct, modern example of biotechnology (a fungus fermented industrially to produce a food product), which is exactly what G10-L-6's 'explain the term biotechnology and provide examples' facet (product|process|ferment) asks for — it teaches a genuine process+product biotech example, not a bare keyword. The previously-considered G10-L-7 (traditional fermentation like cheese/vinegar/nata de coco) was correctly excluded by the prior reviewer since Quorn is industrial, not traditional — G10-L-6 asks for biotechnology examples generally and has no 'traditional' restriction, so it fits without that conflict. Other candidates (G3-L-3 'grow' via 'grown', G3-E-2 'made', G7-L-5 'grow' via 'grown') are keyword hijacks unrelated to their competencies. Translations are faithful. Fusarium venenatum mycoprotein production for Quorn is well-documented and accurate. Parent consolidation verification: Fusarium fermentation producing mycoprotein is an explicit biotechnology process example. Translations faithful. Manufacturer confirms organism/process: https://www.quorn.co.uk/news/how-is-quorn-made . Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20014.review.jsonl

fwg-animal-echolocation-1957.notes: The card depicts a genuine predation interaction in the natural environment — a predator (bat) locating prey (flying insects) — which is exactly the kind of interaction G6-L-6's predation facet (pattern predat|prey) is meant to illustrate, not a bare mention of the word 'prey'. Competing candidates were rejected as hijacks: G4-L-3 aerial-habitat facet matches 'fly' inside 'flying' but the card doesn't classify by habitat; G4-F-8/F-9/F-10 and G6-F-9 match 'sound' but the card doesn't teach non-contact effects, energy forms, community energy use, or wave types — it's specifically about a predator-prey sensing mechanism; G5-L-4 insects facet matches the word 'insects' but the card describes bat behavior, not insect characteristics. Translations are faithful and natural. Bat echolocation to detect insect prey is standard, well-established biology. Parent consolidation verification: Echoes from insect prey helping bats locate food explain predation rather than just mentioning prey. All translations retain the mechanism. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20014.review.jsonl

fwg-light-refraction-1137.notes: The card identifies a natural event observable in the local environment (a rainbow over Baguio after a rain shower) and explains that it is explainable by science (refraction/dispersion of sunlight by water droplets) — exactly the Grade 3 Quarter 1 competency of identifying local objects/activities/natural events that can be explained by science. This is standard, uncontested optics (differential refraction of sunlight by droplets produces the rainbow's colors). Tagalog and Cebuano are faithful, natural renderings of the English at grade-appropriate register. Only the single admitted facet (local-examples) is relied on and is genuinely taught. Parent consolidation verification: Rainbows after local rain explained through refraction/separation are a substantive local natural-event science example. All translations retain the explanation; only local-examples admitted. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20015.review.jsonl

fwg-natural-hazards-167.notes: The card teaches the natural-warning-sign evacuation procedure central to G7-E-8 ('what procedures can be implemented should a tsunami impact a community'): recognizing sudden recession of ocean water during an earthquake as a natural tsunami precursor and immediately evacuating to higher ground. This is the single admitted facet for G7-E-8 and is fully satisfied. Verified against tsunami-safety sources: NOAA/Ready.gov confirm that unusual sudden recession of the sea is a genuine natural warning sign of an incoming tsunami and that the correct response is to immediately move to higher ground or inland, since the wave can arrive within seconds to minutes. Tagalog and Cebuano translations are faithful to the English (humupa=recede, tumakbo agad sa mas mataas na lugar / dali-dali pag-dagan padulong sa taas nga lugar = immediately run to higher ground), age-appropriate for grade 7. Parent consolidation verification: Sudden sea withdrawal associated with an earthquake warrants immediate evacuation to higher ground. This directly supports tsunami evacuation; translations preserve urgency. The statement is treated as protective response to a natural warning, not a forecasting guarantee. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20015.review.jsonl

fwg2-density-comparison-2365.notes: G3-M-9 asks students to identify properties of metals used by the local community, including gold. Density (how heavy gold is for its size, framed here as 'one cup of gold weighs as much as 19 cups of water') is a genuine, concrete physical property of gold, correctly stated and understandable at grade 3 without technical vocabulary. The sole admitted facet for this code is 'gold' (pattern 'gold'), and the card is squarely about that metal's property, not a bare mention of the noun. Tagalog and Cebuano copy are faithful, natural, and grade-appropriate. The fact is verified against an authoritative source: gold's density is 19.32 g/cm3 vs. water's 1.00 g/cm3, i.e. about 19.3 times denser — matching 'about 19 times' and the '19 cups' comparison exactly. Parent consolidation verification: Gold density compared with equal volumes of water is an explicit metal property, covered by G3-M-9 properties AND uses (a card need not teach both). Approximate19-fold value and translations are sound. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20015.review.jsonl

fwg2-saliva-solution-2608.notes: G5-L-1 asks students to identify digestive-system parts including the mouth and describe how they work. The card correctly teaches how the mouth works in digestion: saliva, an aqueous solution containing enzymes, begins the chemical breakdown of solid carbohydrates (accurate — salivary amylase). This is grade-5-appropriate and the only admitted facet for this code (mouth) is genuinely taught. Tagalog/Cebuano are faithful, direct renderings of the same content with no meaning drift. Parent consolidation verification: Salivary enzymes beginning carbohydrate breakdown in the mouth directly teach digestive mouth function. Solid carbohydrates is simplified food context, not a claim all carbohydrate types are salivary substrates. Translations agree. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20016.review.jsonl

fwg2-sun-and-skin-133.notes: The card explains a harmful effect of ultraviolet radiation (a type of electromagnetic radiation) on a living thing (human skin) — sunburn and elevated skin-cancer risk — which is exactly the teaching component of G9-F-13 ('gather information...to explain the harmful effects that EMR can have on living things'). The single admitted facet for this code (focus-1, pattern ioniz|sunburn|ultraviolet) is genuinely taught via the card's sunburn/skin-cancer content, not a stray keyword hit. Skin being the body's largest organ and UV causing sunburn/skin cancer are uncontested facts. Tagalog ('Nakakasira ito! Nagdudulot ang rays na ito ng sunburns at nagpapataas ng risk sa skin cancer, kaya mag-protect tayo sa labas') and Cebuano ('Makadaut kini! Magdala ang rays og sunburns ug mopataas sa risgo sa skin cancer, mao nga mag-protect ta kung mogawas') are faithful, natural, and grade-9 appropriate. Only one variant exists (identical text in app and merged pools), so identity is not in question. Parent consolidation verification: UV skin damage, sunburn and increased cancer risk directly teach harmful EMR effects. All translations preserve the risk rather than asserting every exposure causes cancer. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20016.review.jsonl

grass-grows-from-base-g7.notes: G3-L-3 ('describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce') admits this card via its sole 'grow' facet. The card directly and concretely demonstrates growth as a living-thing characteristic — grass keeps growing back after being eaten or cut — which is a genuine, age-appropriate example of 'living things grow,' not a mere keyword mention. Other candidates (G3-M-8 'cut', G7-L-5 'growth|repair', G7-L-10 'grass' substring) are keyword collisions on cutting/mitosis/food-pyramids that the card does not teach. Translations are faithful in both TL and BIS. The botanical claim (grasses regrow from a basal growth point rather than the tip, allowing survival after grazing/mowing) is accurate. Parent consolidation verification: Grass regrowth from basal growing regions after grazing/cutting is a meaningful living-growth example. Translations retain it. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20017.review.jsonl

grasshopper-incomplete-molting-mechanism.notes: G3-L-3's sole 'grow' facet is genuinely taught: the card's very question is 'How does a grasshopper grow bigger?' and it answers with a concrete growth mechanism (molting), a clear, age-appropriate instance of the living-thing characteristic 'grow'. Other candidates are pure keyword collisions: G4-F-1 and G9-M-11 fire on 'hard' (rigid/soft objects, bonding hardness — unrelated), G8-M-10/G9-M-3 fire on 'outer' (valence electrons, unrelated), G7-L-5 fires on 'growth|repair' (mitosis/meiosis, unrelated), G7-L-10 fires on the 'grass' substring inside 'grasshopper' (food pyramids, unrelated). Translations (TL/BIS) are faithful. The entomology claim (insects have a rigid exoskeleton that doesn't grow, requiring periodic molting to increase in size) is accurate. Parent consolidation verification: Grasshopper moulting to permit growth explicitly illustrates growth of a living animal. New exoskeleton formation is simplified but substantive; translations retain the mechanism. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20017.review.jsonl

gravity-attracts-all-masses-g7.notes: G7-F-1 ('identify that forces act between objects') admits this card via its 'interaction' facet, and the card genuinely teaches that facet: gravity is presented explicitly as a pulling force acting between any two objects with mass — a textbook example of a force acting between objects, appropriate to grade 7. This is distinct from a blanket 'gravity' keyword remapping: I did not recover under G9-F-4 (Newton's third law) because the card never states the forces are equal-and-opposite in a paired sense, only that mutual pulling occurs, so that facet is not genuinely taught. Translations (TL/BIS) are faithful. The physics claim (universal gravitation between all masses, imperceptible at small scales) is correct. Parent consolidation verification: Gravitational pulling between masses illustrates force as interaction between objects. Translations preserve the weak-small-object versus obvious-Earth contrast. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20017.review.jsonl

hotness-or-coldness-g4.notes: The card gives the basic definition of temperature as a characteristic used to describe the weather (degree of hotness/coldness of the air, varying with time of day and weather conditions), which is exactly the teaching component G4-E-4 requires ('identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature...'). The single admitted facet for this code, G4-E-4:temperature, is genuinely taught — the card is entirely about defining temperature. This card is itself sourced from DepEd's own grade-4 competency S4ES-IVe-5 (weather instruments/components), confirming grade and domain alignment. Tagalog ('Ang temperature ay ang antas ng init o lamig ng hangin sa paligid natin...') and Cebuano ('Ang temperature mao ang sukod sa kainit o kabugnaw sa hangin sa atong palibut...') are faithful, natural, and grade-appropriate translations of the English. Single variant, no identity issue. The claim (temperature = degree of hotness/coldness of air, which varies by time of day/weather) is a standard, uncontroversial scientific definition appropriate for grade 4. Parent consolidation verification: Air temperature as hotness/coldness varying with time/weather directly teaches the temperature weather element. All languages agree. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20017.review.jsonl

ice-box-keeps-cold-g5.notes: G3-M-1 asks students to identify objects in the local environment that can be explained by science. An ice box (a common home cooler) keeping ice frozen is exactly that: a local object whose behavior is explained by insulation blocking outside heat so the ice does not melt. Only the single admitted facet (local-examples; pattern melt) is used, and melting is genuinely the process being prevented, not a stray keyword. Tagalog and Cebuano faithfully render insulated walls blocking outside heat so ice does not melt. Claim is standard heat-transfer fact. Parent consolidation verification: Insulated ice-box walls reducing heat entry provide an explanation of a familiar local object. Keep outside heat out is a reasonable functional simplification; no claim of perfect eternal insulation. All translations agree. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20018.review.jsonl

kalaw-eats-figs-favorite-g5.notes: G3-L-7 is met by a concrete interdependence-for-food example: the kalaw/hornbill depends on fig/balete fruit as a favorite food and gathers at fruiting trees to feast. Only the food-and-shelter facet is admitted and it is genuinely taught (foods/feast), not a 'heat'/'feather' substring trap. Fig–hornbill feeding is a well-documented tropical-forest relationship. TL and BIS use kalaw, balete/igos, and kumain/mokaon faithfully. Parent consolidation verification: Hornbills depending on fruiting fig trees for food directly teaches food dependence in a forest. Complete translations preserve both organism and resource. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20018.review.jsonl

light-and-sound-similarity-g4.notes: G6-F-4 is 'identify that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver'. The card's teaching point — light and sound are forms of energy that travel in waves — is a sound component of the 'transfer' facet (pattern energy). The sibling 'source-receiver' facet does not match, so the card will not be swallowed into a source/receiver activity it does not teach. G6-F-9 would admit both longitudinal (sound) and transverse (light) without distinguishing wave types, so it is not assigned. G4-F-9 would also match the 'change' facet via 'because'→'cause', a false hit, so it is not assigned. TL/BIS keep 'waves' in English but correctly say both are forms of energy that travel that way. Single identity. Parent consolidation verification: Light and sound transferring energy in waves directly supports wave-energy transfer. All languages retain the comparison. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20019.review.jsonl

linnaeus-father-classification-g8.notes: G4-M-1 is 'use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s'. The card identifies Carl Linnaeus as the scientist who created the modern way of naming living things — a foreign scientist plus the binomial/naming system as the created work. Only the 'invention' facet (invent|develop|creat) matches; the 'sources' facet does not, so no biography/museum activity credit. G5-L-4 (classification table) and G8-L-6 (six-kingdom/three-domain) are not taught and are not assigned. TL/BIS correctly credit Linnaeus with creating the modern naming method. Single identity. Parent consolidation verification: Linnaeus and the modern naming system identify a scientist with a specific devised scientific method, a useful scientist/contribution example. Only invention admitted; translations preserve attribution without stray classification facets. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20019.review.jsonl

liver-makes-bile-digest-fat-g6.notes: G4-L-1 asks students to describe in simple terms how the digestive (among other) human body systems work. The card teaches a digestive-system component: the liver makes bile that helps break down fat in food, matching the sole admitted G4-L-1 facet 'digestive' (digest|break.*food). Muscular/skeletal/circulatory/respiratory facets do not match, so there is no false-system admission. G5-L-1 and G8-L-1 require pictures/labeled-diagram tracing of listed gut parts and are not assigned. TL 'apdo'/'pagtunaw ng taba' and BIS 'apdo'/'pagtunaw sa tambok' correctly mean bile breaking down fat. Single identity. Parent consolidation verification: Liver-produced bile helping fat breakdown is a simple digestive-system function component; helps allows emulsification rather than claiming bile is a digestive enzyme. All translations agree. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20019.review.jsonl

mantis-shrimp-tatampal-g6.notes: G6-L-6 asks students to describe that living things interact through predation. This card is a concrete, verified predation example: the Philippine tatampal (mantis shrimp) strikes so hard it cracks its prey's shell — the whole sentence is the predator–prey interaction, not a stray noun hit on 'prey'. The only admitted facet for this code is G6-L-6:predation (pattern predat|prey) and it is genuinely taught. Other admitted codes are keyword coincidences (G4-F-1 'hard' rigid/soft objects; G4-F-4 'fast' speed graphs; G8-M-2/M-8 'shell' electron shells; G9-M-10 'sea' of electrons; G9-M-11 'hard' bonding properties) and were rejected. Claim is accurate (stomatopod dactyl-club strikes can fracture mollusc shells). TL/BIS faithfully render tatampal, strike, prey, and hard shell at a grade-appropriate register. Single identical variant in both pools. Parent consolidation verification: Mantis-shrimp strike cracking prey shells provides a concrete predation mechanism. All languages agree. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20020.review.jsonl

maya-bird-g3.notes: G3-L-7 is 'observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs'. The card is a local, grade-3-appropriate observed example: the Philippine maya depends on other living things (seeds and tiny insects) for food around homes and farms. Only one facet of this code is admitted (G3-L-7:food-and-shelter) and the food half is genuinely taught. Rejected G3-L-6:shelter (the word 'homes' is where the bird is seen, not shelter-as-a-need), G5-L-4:insects (no classification table), G5-L-6:birds (no life-cycle comparison), and the many Philippin-keyword Earth/energy hits. Diet claim is standard (maya/tree sparrow eats seeds and insects). TL ('kumakain ito ng buto at maliliit na insekto') and BIS ('mokaon kini og mga liso ug gagmay nga insekto') are faithful. Single identical variant in both pools. Parent consolidation verification: Maya eating seeds/insects near homes/farms directly supplies food dependence. Complete translations agree. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20020.review.jsonl

molars-grind-leaves-g5.notes: G3-L-4 asks students to observe outer body parts of animals and identify their role in moving and gathering food; the authored feeding facet (beak|mouth|teeth|tongue) exists specifically for feeding parts. This card teaches that cows' and horses' molar teeth grind tough grass — teeth as a body part whose role is gathering/processing food — so the only admitted facet (G3-L-4:feeding) is genuinely taught. Rejected G4-L-7 (no labeled food chain) and G8-L-1 (no digestive-tract diagram). Hypsodont molars for grinding forage are standard ungulate anatomy. TL ('malalaking bagang na gumigiling ng matigas na damo') and BIS ('dagkong bagang nga sige og galing sa gahi nga sagbot') are faithful. Single identical variant in both pools. Parent consolidation verification: Broad molars grinding fibrous grass directly explain a feeding body-part function. All languages preserve teeth, action and food. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20020.review.jsonl

mudskipper-eats-during-low-tide-g5.notes: G3-L-7 is 'observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs'. The card is exactly such an example: a mangrove mudskipper (familiar in Philippine tidal flats) depends on the low-tide environment to reach the food hiding in the exposed mud. Only the food-and-shelter facet is admitted for this code, and the card genuinely teaches the food-dependence half, not a bare keyword. Tagalog ('kapag kati at nakalantad ang putik, dahil dito makikita ang pagkain nito') and Cebuano ('kon mohunas ug madayag ang lapok, kay didto makit-an ang iyang pagkaon') are faithful. G3-L-6:food is not chosen: the card does not list food as a generic basic need; it shows environmental dependence for food. G5-L-9/G6-L-7 remain related_only (no adaptation mechanism; no biotic/abiotic classification). Parent consolidation verification: Low tide exposing mud where mudskippers obtain food explicitly links feeding to environmental conditions. Translations retain it; only food-and-shelter admitted. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20021.review.jsonl

night-sky-as-a-clock-g6.notes: G3-E-8 is 'explain how natural objects in the sky affect activities of people'. The card teaches that familiar star groups rising and setting were used to track night hours — a natural clock — which is exactly sky objects affecting a human activity (timekeeping). Only the nighttime facet is admitted (not daytime), and that is the content taught. Claim is historically accurate. Tagalog ('Ang pag-akyat at paglubog ng mga kilalang bituin ay nagtatala ng oras sa gabi') and Cebuano ('Ang pagsaka ug paglubog sa mga pamilyar nga bituon nagtala sa oras sa gabii') are faithful. G3-E-7 is not chosen: it would also admit the record-motion activity facet on 'tracked', which the card does not teach as a student recording/sketching activity. G6-E-10 remains related_only (no indigenous-Philippine secondary-source investigation). Parent consolidation verification: Using rising/setting star groups to track hours directly shows sky objects affecting a human timekeeping activity. All languages agree. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20021.review.jsonl

ocean-food-chain-plankton-g5.notes: G3-L-7 requires observed examples of living things depending on one another to meet basic needs. The card is a compact food-chain example of that dependence: plankton eaten by small fish eaten by bigger fish. Only the food-and-shelter facet is admitted for this code, and the eating relationships are what the card teaches. Claim is the standard marine grazing food chain (accurate at grade 3). Tagalog and Cebuano render the same who-eats-whom chain faithfully. G4-L-7/G6-L-5/G7-L-9 remain related_only (no Philippine labeled herbivore/carnivore/omnivore chain, no producer/consumer/decomposer roles, no trophic-level energy pyramid). G3-E-6:stars is a substring hijack on 'start' and is not chosen. Parent consolidation verification: Plankton-to-small-fish-to-large-fish sequence is a sound introductory example of food dependence; it need not reproduce every marine food-web exception. Translations preserve sequence. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20021.review.jsonl

owl-diet-rodents-g4.notes: G3-L-7 ('observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs') admits only the food-and-shelter facet (pattern food|eat|shelter); the environment facet (water|soil|air|sun) does not match. The card is a concrete, age-appropriate example of one living thing depending on others for food: owls eat rats, mice, insects, and other small animals. Same teaching shape as later-set diet recoveries (draco-eats-ants, eel-carnivore). G5-L-4:insects is a classification-table competency and is not taught. TL kuwago/kumakain ng daga, insekto, maliliit na hayop and BIS bukaw/mokaon og ilaga, insekto, gagmay nga mananap keep the meaning (mice folded into daga/ilaga). No variant split. Parent consolidation verification: Owls eating rodents/insects/other animals directly teaches animal-food dependence with an appropriate most qualifier. Translations agree. palawan-peacock-diet-g5.notes: G3-L-7 admits only food-and-shelter; environment does not match. pawikan-eat-jellyfish-seagrass-g4.notes: G3-L-7 admits only food-and-shelter; environment (water|soil|air|sun) does not fire on seagrass/jellyfish. The card teaches that sea turtles (pawikan) depend on other living things for food, with two real diet paths (seagrass vs jellyfish). G3-L-6:food would swallow this into 'identify food as a basic need' without that framing, so it is not tagged. TL pawikan/damong-dagat/dikya and BIS pawikan/damong-dagat/dikya keep the meaning. planting-trees-helps-g3.notes: G3-L-8 is 'recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive'. The card states a concrete Grade 3 care action (planting trees) as a way to protect and conserve the environment — exactly the care-actions component, and planting trees is also the habitat-protection action that unit is built around (trees as living habitat). Both currently matching facets of this code (care-actions: plant|protect|conserv; protect-habitats: tree) are genuinely taught, not stray keywords. Claim is correct. Other matches (G3-M-1 'plant', G3-L-2 'tree', G3-L-6 'shelter', G4-E-2/E-9 'plant', G5-E-1/E-6, G6-E-5/E-6/E-9, G8-F-9 'conservation', G9-L-8/L-11, G10-E-11) are keyword-only. TL 'pagtatanim ng mga puno... maprotektahan at mapangalagaan ang kapaligiran' and BIS 'pagtanom ug mga kahoy... mapanalipdan ug maampingan ang palibot' are faithful and natural. Single identical variant in both pools. Parent consolidation verification: Tree planting as environmental care directly supports both care actions and habitat protection. A simple action component is appropriate; translations agree. Evidence: tools/curriculum-recovery/batch-20023.review.jsonl

plants-store-light-as-chemical-g6.notes: G4-E-9 is 'make suggestions about the importance of the Sun to living things'. The card teaches that plants use sunlight and store it as chemical energy in the food they make — a core, accurate reason the Sun matters to living things (the importance facet). Only that facet of G4-E-9 is admitted (sources-discussion unmatched), so no discussion/secondary-source activity is credited. Scientifically correct at grade level (light energy converted to chemical energy in food). Not chosen: G8-L-9 is not admitted (no process/raw materials/products); G3-L-7 matches both food-and-shelter and environment, and food-and-shelter is only 'food they make' not animals depending on plants for food/shelter; G6-L-7/G6-L-8/G4-F-9/F-10 are keyword hits on light/energy. TL/BIS faithfully render 'chemical energy' as kemikal na enerhiya / kemikal nga enerhiya and sunlight as liwanag ng araw / kahayag sa adlaw. Variants identical.
